articles.title_original: Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case - media reports
articles.title_zh: Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case - media reports
facts_zh:
Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case - media reports
- Published
A Massachusetts judge has denied motions to dismiss the murder case of Lindsay Clancy, the US woman accused of murdering her three children, according to local US media.
The judge's ruling comes after Clancy's defence team requested dismissal of the case after her first trial ended in a mistrial in September, when a 12-person jury failed to reach a consensus.
The ruling clears the way for prosecutors to pursue the case.

all_titles.en: Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case - media reports

articles.title_original: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
articles.title_zh: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
facts_zh:
France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
- Published
France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month.
Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions.
Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.

all_titles.en: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking

articles.title_zh: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction
facts_zh:
Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction
Russia's leading independent newspaper has closed after being evicted from its offices and facing pressure from authorities.
For 30 years, Novaya Gazeta published investigations into corruption, human rights violations and abuse of power in the country.
On Monday, the team behind the newspaper had a final editorial meeting before packing up their belongings and leaving.

all_titles.en: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction

articles.title_zh: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine
facts_zh:
Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine
- Published
Nine Zimbabweans have been arrested in South Africa after they were caught allegedly trying to leave the country to fight in the war between Russia and the Ukraine, police say.
The group, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in and around Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team on Sunday evening.
They were caught as they were "preparing to board flights out of the country", authorities added, but their final destination is unclear.

articles.title_zh: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
facts_zh:
At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
- Published
At least 39 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports.
The interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established.
The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands.

all_titles.en: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal

articles.title_zh: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
facts_zh:
Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
- Published
A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow, and his parents and sister at their home, died in hospital early on Monday, Polish police have said.
The 24-year-old, who has been named as Michal Oksinski by local media, was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday, police said.
Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.

all_titles.en: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say

articles.title_zh: Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
facts_zh:
Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
- Published
Three children and one woman were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in central Gaza following heavy rain, the Hamas-run health ministry says.
Five injured people were also reportedly rescued after the incident on Sunday night at a camp for displaced families south of Deir al-Balah.
Videos showed men using phone torches to search for survivors beneath boulders, sand and collapsed tents.
